incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER — Severity: P1. multi-gpu training job 9345 in prod-ephemeral experienced NCCL communicator timeout (rank 2 -> rank 3). Auto-escalation to oncall. job_id=9345 cluster=tp-pool-7
Alex (oncall): ack. pulling logs now. any customer impact noted?
Luis (cs): seeing 4 active customer inference streams fail with 503s, roughly 12 jobs retried. Customers A and C opened support tickets. tagging here. :sad_panda:
Priya (runtime): looking at node logs. dmesg shows consecutive Xid 79s and then container OOM kill. likely CUDA driver GPU reset + container exit. snippets below.
Priya (runtime): ```
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: GPU 0000:65:00.0: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, PID=23456, GPU has fallen off the bus
[ 1234.568100] audit: type=1701 audit(1612345678.123:456): auid=4294967295 uid=0 gid=0 ses=4294967295 comm="python" exe="/usr/bin/python3" sig=9 res=1
Nov 03 12:34:56 node-72 kubelet[1234]: Container "trainer-9345" exited with status 137 (OOMKilled)
```
Sam (ml-infra): stacktrace from NCCL process shows timeout in ncclCommInitRank -> allreduce at step 1023, then watchdog triggered. looks like communicator lost peer after GPU reset.
Alex (oncall): is this isolated to node-72 or multi-node? Priya?
Priya (runtime): mostly node-72, but one other host had a brief heartbeat drop. NVLink links on node-72 show errors. suspect hardware flake triggered by memory spike + driver state.
Sam (ml-infra): immediate mitigations: 1) cordon node-72, 2) drain pods and restart trainer containers, 3) scale up spare tp-pool instances and route traffic to them, 4) roll back to lower batch-size model variant for affected customers to reduce memory.
Alex (oncall): doing cordon+drain now. ```kubectl cordon node-72 && kubectl drain node-72 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data``` Will restart containers on healthy nodes.
Priya (runtime): restarting container isn't enough if driver state on host is bad. we should reboot node-72 after drain. I'll open a host reboot ticket with infra.
Sam (ml-infra): I'll trigger autoscale and move 2 reserved instances into tp-pool-7: runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/tp-node-failover
Luis (cs): customer note: sending interim message to affected customers about degraded throughput and automatic retries. ETA to full recovery ~ 15-30 mins. updating tickets.
Priya (runtime): temp mitigation: enable model fallback routing for route "inference/v1/pipeline-x" -> hit dedicated fallback pool (lower perf but stable). Applying route override now.
Alex (oncall): applied route override. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: ACTION_LOG: node-72 cordoned, pods drained, route override applied, autoscale triggered. Incident state: mitigation-in-progress.
Priya (runtime): after drain, host dmesg still shows intermittent ECC corrected errors on PCIe. infra indicates firmware update pending for node-72 hardware. tagging infra oncall.
Sam (ml-infra): also enabling a temporary NCCL retry override env var for trainer to allow communicator re-init on transient peer loss: NCCL_NTHREADS=8 NCCL_DEBUG=INFO NCCL_COMM_RETRY=3 (see runbook)
Alex (oncall): sequence of ops executed: cordon+drain @1769001290, route override @1769001320, autoscale up @1769001350, host reboot scheduled @1769001380.
Maya (oncall-next): thanks Alex, I'm taking over monitoring. will watch customer tickets and confirm until host back and we verify stable runs. ping me for handoff.
Luis (cs): summarizing customer impact: ~12 affected jobs, degraded latency for 4 active streams, no data leakage, retries in progress. CS outreach in motion.
Priya (runtime): post-reboot we'll run a smoke job and check nccl allreduce stability across tp partitions. plan to leave route fallback for 1 hour post-green-check.
Alex (oncall): good. handing off to Maya (oncall-next) for next 30m watch. I'll remain available if escalation needed. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: INCIDENT_UPDATE: severity=P1 -> mitigated (degraded). next update expected in 30m or earlier if regressions.
Maya (oncall-next): ack, monitoring. final note: create follow-up issue to replace node-72 NIC module and schedule firmware window. assigning to infra team.
